title: Mathematics Practice Test 2 - Mathematics - Coordinate Geometry (Lines)
subject: Mathematics

questions.q: Let the slope of $3x + 2y = 5$ be $m_1$, and the slope of $6x + 4y = 7$ be $m_2$. Which of the following is true?
questions.explain: Convert both equations into slope-intercept form ($y = mx + b$). For the first equation, $3x + 2y = 5$ transforms to $2y = -3x + 5$, then $y = -\frac{3}{2}x + \frac{5}{2}$. So $m_1 = -\frac{3}{2}$. For the second equation, $6x + 4y = 7$ transforms to $4y = -6x + 7$, then $y = -\frac{6}{4}x + \frac{7}{4}$. Simplifying $-\frac{6}{4}$ yields $y = -\frac{3}{2}x + \frac{7}{4}$. So $m_2 = -\frac{3}{2}$. Because both slopes are $-\frac{3}{2}$, $m_1 = m_2$.
